headline: This 2016 law sets up planning and coordination rules for moving power from one President to the next and adds several reporting requirements.
what_it_does: The law requires the President to plan for an orderly transfer of power, including a White House transition council set up at least six months before an election and an agency transition directors council. It requires the General Services Administration to name a Federal Transition Coordinator and requires each agency to name a senior career employee to oversee transition work. It also adds reports on presidential records funding, political appointees moving into civil service jobs, late-term regulations, and transition security threats.

who_it_affects.group: Eligible presidential candidates and their transition teams
who_it_affects.how: They get a designated liaison and a memorandum of understanding that sets the terms for transition staff access to agency employees, facilities, and documents.
Each agency must name one senior career employee to manage transition activities, and GSA must name a senior career appointee as Federal Transition Coordinator.
It must carry out its presidential transition duties and make sure agencies follow transition planning and reporting requirements.

who_it_affects.group: The National Archives and Records Administration
who_it_affects.how: The President's budget request must include funding for managing presidential records in the final year of a presidential term.

who_it_affects.group: Political appointees seeking civil service jobs
who_it_affects.how: The Office of Personnel Management must report on agency requests to move political or former political appointees into nonpolitical civil service positions, quarterly in the final year of a term.
The Government Accountability Office must report on significant final rules issued in the last 120 days of certain administrations, which the law defines by economic, safety, and policy impact.
It must send Congress a report analyzing threats and vulnerabilities the country faces during a presidential transition.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was signed March 18, 2016, and the summary does not give a separate effective date, so some duties apply starting with the next presidential transition and reporting deadlines follow the timelines written in each section.
